findings.evidence: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Modular.lean:367 `def fd : Set ℍ := {z | 1 ≤ normSq (z : ℂ) ∧ |z.re| ≤ 1/2}` (closed, contains `I` and `ρ`); Orbits.lean:120-121 `(hnorm : ∀ z ∈ X, 1 < ‖z‖)`; ValencePV.lean:541 index `↑(T \ ({Complex.I, (ρ : ℂ), (ρ : ℂ) + 1} : Finset ℂ))`; roadmap ModularForms/README.md Layer 1: "the sum running over the non-elliptic SL₂(ℤ)-orbits of ℍ".
findings.fix: State the restriction: the step closes the gap only for divisor sets whose nonzero-order points all lie in `𝒟ᵒ`, i.e. for forms with no elliptic/boundary zeros; otherwise the completeness hypothesis must be relativised to non-elliptic orbits. Drop "whole orbit space" in favour of "non-elliptic orbit space" where the downstream sum is meant.
findings.issue: "This is what promotes that lemma's image-indexed ∑ᶠ to the whole orbit space" overclaims. `hX` quantifies over the *closed* `𝒟`, but `sum_orderOfVanishingAt_ofComplex_eq_finsum_orbit` forces `X ⊆ 𝒟ᵒ` (`1 < ‖z‖`, `|z.re| < 1/2`, lines 120-121), and its real consumer indexes over `↑(T \ {I, ρ, ρ+1})` (ValencePV.lean:539-541). So `hX` cannot hold whenever `f` has a nonzero-order point on `∂𝒟` — `i`, `ρ`, or any arc zero, i.e. every Eisenstein series. The docstring presents the chaining as unconditional and says "whole orbit space" where the roadmap target is the *non-elliptic* orbit space.

findings.evidence: Orbits.lean:34-36 versus Orbits.lean:120-121 and ValencePV.lean:539-541 as above.
findings.fix: Shorten the bullet to what the statement delivers (an orbit missed by a divisor set complete over `𝒟` has order zero) without asserting the extension is thereby achieved.

summary: The new docstring overclaims that this lemma promotes the image-indexed sum to the whole orbit space: its completeness hypothesis ranges over the closed 𝒟 while the lemma it names constrains X to 𝒟ᵒ and the real consumer deletes i and ρ, so hX is unsatisfiable exactly for the forms the valence formula targets. A second paragraph documents the proof rather than the result.
